linux-amd.review: Generated C maps f67 to numeric ad.push and f108 to managed ad.push-owned. Numeric capacity hits bypass growth; growth uses two realloc calls (8*cap and 16*cap), then initialized-region memmoves (8*used and 4*used). Parent stores remain 32-bit and weights 64-bit. Numeric growth has no managed-weight branch. Nested code calls a shared reserve helper that retains both owner branches; its managed path performs one native parent realloc, separate typed weight growth, then parent relocation and capacity publication. Ordinary saved registers and stack spills remain. AMD64 local stack figures exclude saved-register pushes; ARM64 frames include saved registers. No universal register, cache, or timing improvement is inferred.
